message.content:
### Building a New PC – Step‑by‑Step Guide

Below is a practical, beginner‑friendly walkthrough.  
Feel free to skip sections you already know, but keep the order for safety and best results.

| # | What to Do | Why It Matters | Tips |
|---|------------|----------------|------|
| **1** | **Plan & Budget** | Know what you’ll use it for (gaming, video editing, office, etc.) | List required specs: CPU, GPU, RAM, storage, PSU, case, cooling. |
| **2** | **Gather Parts** | All components must be compatible. | Use a PC builder tool (e.g., PCPartPicker) to check compatibility and price. |
| **3** | **Prepare Workspace** | Clean, static‑free area. | Anti‑static wrist strap or work on a non‑conductive mat. |
| **4** | **Open the Case** | Access motherboard, power supply, drives. | Remove side panels; keep screws handy. |
| **5** | **Install the Power Supply (PSU)** | Supplies power to all components. | Align the PSU with the rear mounting rail, screw it in, route cables to the back. |
| **6** | **Mount the Motherboard** | Base for all other components. | Align standoffs with holes, screw firmly. |
| **7** | **Install the CPU** | Central processing unit. | Open the socket latch, align the CPU (triangle marker), gently place, lock latch. |
| **8** | **Apply Thermal Paste & Install CPU Cooler** | Keeps CPU from overheating. | Use a pea‑size amount of paste, spread evenly. Attach cooler per its instructions. |
| **9** | **Insert RAM Modules** | Memory for multitasking. | Open DIMM slots, align notch, press until clicks. |
| **10** | **Mount Storage Drives (SSD/HDD)** | Data storage. | For M.2 SSDs, slide into the M.2 slot and screw. For 2.5”/3.5” drives, use drive bays or brackets. |
| **11** | **Install the Graphics Card (GPU)** | Handles rendering for games, video, etc. | Slide into the top PCI‑e x16 slot, secure with screws, connect any required PCI‑e power cables. |
| **12** | **Connect Power Cables** | Power all components. | 24‑pin ATX to motherboard, 8‑pin EPS to CPU, 6/8‑pin PCI‑e to GPU, SATA power to drives. |
| **13** | **Connect Data Cables** | Data transfer between components. | SATA data cables to motherboard and drives, M.2 data is built‑in. |
| **14** | **Cable Management** | Improves airflow, aesthetics. | Tuck cables behind the motherboard tray, use zip ties or Velcro straps. |
| **15** | **Check All Connections** | Prevent shorts, ensure power. | Verify no loose screws, no stray wires touching metal. |
| **16** | **Close the Case** | Protect components, finish look. | Reattach side panels, secure screws. |
| **17** | **First Boot & BIOS Setup** | Confirm hardware is recognized. | Power on, enter BIOS (usually F2, Del, or Esc). Check CPU, RAM, storage, GPU. Update BIOS if needed. |
| **18** | **Install Operating System (OS)** | Turn your PC into a usable machine. | Create a bootable USB (Windows, Linux, etc.), boot from it, follow installation wizard. |
| **19** | **Install Drivers & Updates** | Ensure hardware works optimally. | Install motherboard chipset drivers, GPU drivers, Wi‑Fi/Bluetooth drivers. Run Windows Update or equivalent. |
| **20** | **Test & Benchmark** | Verify performance, stability. | Run stress tests (Prime95, 3DMark, etc.) and monitor temperatures. |

---

#### Quick Checklist

- **CPU** – Intel i5/i7/i9 or AMD Ryzen 5/7/9
- **Motherboard** – Matching socket, chipset, form factor (ATX, mATX, mini‑ITX)
- **RAM** – 16 GB DDR4/DDR5 (minimum 8 GB for basic use)
- **GPU** – NVIDIA RTX 3060/3070/3080 or AMD Radeon RX 6600/6700/6800
- **Storage** – NVMe SSD (250 GB–1 TB) + optional HDD (1 TB+)
- **PSU** – 550 W–750 W 80+ Gold (adjust for GPU power draw)
- **Case** – ATX mid‑tower or mini‑ITX, good airflow
- **Cooling** – Stock cooler or aftermarket air/liquid cooler
- **Operating System** – Windows 11/10, Ubuntu, etc.

---

#### Common Pitfalls & How to Avoid Them

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| **Shorted components** | Use anti‑static wrist strap; keep screws away from motherboard. |
| **Overheating** | Ensure proper thermal paste application; good case airflow; consider aftermarket cooler. |
| **Boot failure** | Double‑check CPU socket orientation; ensure RAM is seated; verify BIOS settings. |
| **Power issues** | Verify PSU wattage; use correct connectors; avoid overloading PCI‑e slots. |
| **Cable clutter** | Plan cable routing early; use zip ties; keep cables away from fans. |

---

#### Resources

- **PCPartPicker** – Build & price‑compare parts, check compatibility.  
- **YouTube Channels** – Linus Tech Tips, JayzTwoCents, Paul's Hardware for visual guides.  
- **Reddit** – r/buildapc for community support and troubleshooting.  
- **Manufacturer Manuals** – Always read the motherboard, GPU, and PSU manuals for specific instructions.

---

### Final Thought

Building a PC is a rewarding project that gives you full control over performance and aesthetics. Take your time, double‑check every connection, and enjoy the process! If you hit a snag, feel free to ask for help—happy building!
